From time to time I stumble upon area that is tagged as brownfield, but which is used as a parking (sometimes improvised, sometimes organised).
Latest example of organised one I've seen: https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/1087347432
https://www.mapillary.com/app/?pKey=1024894743660992
It is not marked with signs, but with gates present, I don't believe it's an improvised one. So technically land is in use, right?
Should brownfield be removed here, and replaced with parking?
If so, would it also be correct move for improvised parkings organised on unused land?

Way: 1087347432
OpenStreetMap is a map of the world, created by people like you and free to use under an open license.
Mapillary
Street-level imagery, powered by collaboration and computer vision.

Yeah, this is potentially complicated. When does a brownfield stop being a brownfield if the area is "used"? Like, how much area? Is it still functionally a brownfield, just with an extra parking lot? Or has parking replaced the brownfield? Or has the brownfield area been reduced and now it's part brownfield, part parking. I really don't know what I would do.
